exposure: Childbirth complications (umbilical cord prolapse, Meconium aspiration syndrome, failure to descend, acute fetal distress)
outcome: Other causes of hip involvement (Legg-Calve-Perthes disease, epiphysiolysis of the femur head, transient synovitis of the hip, septic hip, tumor, hip dislocation, hip dysplasia)
cohort: The study included 81 children, predominantly male (59.3%), with a mean age of diagnosis of 9.9 years (range 1-16 years), divided into two groups: JIA patients with coxitis (G1) and patients with other causes of hip involvement (G2).
finding: Maternal and perinatal history, including delivery mode, fetal presentation, and birth weight, did not statistically differ between JIA patients with coxitis and patients with other causes of hip involvement.
mod_finding: There was no statistical difference between the JIA with coxitis group and the other hip involvement group regarding delivery mode (P = 0.07) and fetal presentation before birth (P = 0.48).
followup_time: Up to 16 years after birth (age range of diagnosis)
cross-section timing: Data was retrieved from medical records for children diagnosed with hip involvement at a mean age of 9.9 years (range 1-16 years).
birth_weight: Mean birth weight was 3.4 kg (range 1.3-9 kg).
